# PREREG_O -- pass 9, campaign O (sub-cluster grain at a FIXED training-set size)

**Frozen 2026-07-28, while campaign O has ZERO runs.** Base commit c8ef00f. Do not edit this file
after the first run dir under `if_repair/runs/campaigns/O/` exists.

## What motivated this campaign (and why that does not contaminate it)

`p9_stratum_control.py`, run on campaign N's committed data and the frozen
`p7_pooled_oos._graddot("cached")` object, target C5, Kendall tau_b, depth 4:

| scope | n masks | LDS | ceiling | ratio | ratio 95% CI | perm null (mean) | clears 0.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POOLED (the committed primary) | 149 | 0.4747 | 0.6715 | **0.7069** | [0.612, 0.817] | **0.3530** | yes |
| within 4of9 | 56 | 0.2078 | 0.5053 | 0.4112 | [0.092, 0.777] | 0.0009 | no |
| within 5of9 | 37 | 0.2583 | 0.5211 | 0.4956 | [0.115, 0.943] | 0.0022 | no |
| within 6of9 | 56 | 0.1688 | 0.5324 | 0.3171 | [-0.017, 0.719] | -0.0020 | no |

The pooled row reproduces `results/confirm_nseries.csv` exactly, so this is the same computation,
not a competing one.

The permutation null is the finding. Outcomes are shuffled WITHIN stratum and correlated against
GradDot's predictions. GradDot is a **fixed** estimator -- nothing is fit -- so a surviving
correlation cannot be leakage under any definition. Pooled it survives at **0.353** of a real
0.475: |S| in {4,5,6} sets the training set to 60/75/90 demos, that moves the outcome directly, and
every estimator's mask prediction is a SUM over kept demos and so grows with the count as well.
Within stratum the same null collapses to ~0.000, which is what a working control looks like, and
the half-ceiling bar is not cleared in any stratum.

`p8_prereg.md` anticipated exactly this -- "|S| is a stratum, not a covariate to pool over ...
Reported per stratum and pooled with |S| controlled" -- but `confirm_nseries.evaluate` computes the
primary pooled over all 149 conditional masks and uses `st` only in the secondary paired analysis.
The control was promised and not applied to the primary.

**Why that motivation does not contaminate campaign O.** The observation above is a diagnosis of an
existing draw. It selects the hypothesis; it cannot also test it. Campaign O is a fresh draw at a
grain no campaign has touched, its masks are frozen with this file at zero runs, and its design
removes the confound by construction rather than adjusting for it after the fact.

## Hypothesis of record

**FAMILY OF TWO** (one per fresh grain), so **alpha = 0.025 one-sided each** by Bonferroni.

> **O1.** At k = 3, holding the training set at exactly 75 demos and conditioning on all of C5's
> groups retained, `GradDot_dmean` clears the absolute half-ceiling bar: the **lower bound of the
> 95% bootstrap CI of the ratio** is >= 0.5.
>
> **O2.** The same at k = 5.

**The decision rule is the CI lower bound, not a point estimate.** Campaign N's PASS rule combined
a p-value against rho > 0 -- which at n ~ 150 is astronomically significant for any modest positive
tau and therefore not the binding constraint -- with a point-estimate check that ratio >= 0.5. That
attaches alpha to the easy half of the decision and none to the half that carries the claim. Here
the bar itself is the inferential object: masks are resampled and **the ceiling is recomputed on
each resample**, so the CI carries the uncertainty of both the numerator and the denominator.

**Secondary gate, preregistered, not alpha-bearing:** the observed LDS must also exceed the 97.5th
percentile of the within-design permutation null (outcomes shuffled, estimator fixed). At a fixed
training-set size that null should sit at ~0; if it does not, the design has a size channel left in
it and the primary is not interpretable. This is a validity check on the design, reported whatever
it says.

## Statistic

**Primary: Kendall tau_b. Mandatory secondary: Spearman.** Both bars reported under both.

**Fixed by continuity, NOT re-selected at this grain.** BLOCKERS #30 chooses the statistic on
reliability and noise at the grain in question, and pass 8 found the two criteria disagree at
cluster grain where they agreed at demo grain. But the deliverable here is a CURVE across k, and a
curve whose points use different statistics is not a curve. Kendall is what the k=15 rung was
scored under, so Kendall is what all three rungs use. A blind re-selection at k=3/5 is computed and
reported as a check; if it disagrees with Kendall that is a finding about the grain, and it does not
change the primary.

## Design

**Fixed training-set size: exactly 75 retained demos on every mask, at every grain.** This is the
campaign's reason to exist. |S| variation is not controlled after the fact -- it does not exist.

| rung | groups | mask keeps | mask space | source | n masks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| k = 3 | 45 (5/cluster) | 25 of 45 | C(40,20) ~ 1.4e11 | campaign O, fresh | 400 |
| k = 5 | 27 (3/cluster) | 15 of 27 | C(24,12) ~ 2.7e6 | campaign O, fresh | 400 |
| k = 15 | 9 (= clusters) | 5 of 9 | C(8,4) = 70 | campaign N 5of9, **on disk** | 37 |

`k = 1` is **not** a rung. Demo-grain masks retain 7-8 demos of every cluster and never remove one
whole (`src/masks.py` stratification), so they are a different removal geometry rather than the same
estimand at smaller k. Shown as a labelled reference only, carrying no alpha.

**Conditioning: ALL of C5's groups retained** -- 5 of 5 at k=3, 3 of 3 at k=5, the whole cluster at
k=15. This is the sub-cluster reading of campaign N's "target-in-mask", fixed here rather than left
to the implementer, because ">= 1 group retained" is a different estimand with a different n.

**Balance by construction.** Masks are built in complementary pairs: permute the non-target groups,
take the first half for one mask and the last half for its partner. After R rounds every non-target
group has appeared in exactly R masks. Measured spread = **0** at both grains; every free group
appears in exactly 200 of 400 masks. No swap-repair loop is involved.

**Disjointness.** A sub-cluster mask whose groups tile five whole clusters would be a campaign-N
|S|=5 signature. Asserted against Stage F's and campaign N's demo-set signatures; 0 collisions at
both grains.

**Depth: 2, job list SEED-MAJOR, seed slots {4401, 4402}.** Even, as BLOCKERS #39 requires for the
split-half ceiling to be non-NaN. Allocation-optimal per BLOCKERS #29, whose demo-grain curve is
used here **as a stated proxy** -- there are no sub-cluster outcomes in the repo to resample, so
unlike pass 8 the allocation cannot be re-derived at this grain, and saying so is part of the
prereg. Seed-major means every prefix is a complete balanced design.

**Depth is MATCHED across the curve.** The k=15 rung is re-derived from campaign N restricted to the
same two seed slots. Comparing a depth-2 rung to campaign N's committed depth-4 number would confound
grain with protocol: `ratio` is not depth-invariant (the ceiling rises with depth, and the ratio is
rho/r where the attainable maximum is ~sqrt(r), so lower depth inflates the ratio). The committed
0.7069 at depth 4 is used only as a code-correctness regression, never as a curve point.

Total GPU: 800 masks x depth 2 = **1600 retrains**, ~18.2 h wall at campaign N's measured 88/hour.

## Stopping rule (prespecified, outcome-blind)

Campaign O is time-boxed. **The analysis uses the largest EVEN depth d such that all masks of that
grain have d completed seeds**, read off the run directory and never off the outcomes. With depth 2
planned, this is 2 or the campaign does not analyse. No optional stopping.

## Scored exactly once

`confirm_oseries.py` refuses to overwrite an existing result file, following `confirm_nseries.py`.

## Decision rule for every outcome pattern (preregistered)

| pattern | reading |
|---|---|
| O1 and O2 both clear | crossover is at or below k=3; report a bound, not a point |
| O2 clears, O1 does not | crossover in (3, 5]; the interpolated estimate is the deliverable |
| neither clears, k=15 does | crossover in (5, 15] |
| neither clears, k=15 does not either | at a fixed training-set size, attribution is not measurable at ANY grain on this corpus -- the pass-8 headline was the |S| effect, and that is pass 9's result |
| O1 clears, O2 does not | non-monotone; treat as a partition or design artifact and investigate before reporting |
| permutation null non-zero at fixed size | design still has a size channel; primary not interpretable, report and stop |

## Secondary and descriptive (no alpha, no inferential claim)

- The four frozen corrections vs `GradDot_dmean` at both fresh grains -- does the pass-8 reversal
  (BLOCKERS #37) reproduce at sub-cluster grain?
- The datamodel at both fresh grains, leave-one-mask-out.
- Blind statistic re-selection at k=3/5, as a check on the fixed-Kendall choice.
- `rho/sqrt(ceiling)` alongside `rho/ceiling` at every rung, since the ceiling is a reliability and
  the attainable maximum is ~sqrt(r).
- The across-cluster composition arm is **NOT built** in campaign O. It would need its own retrains
  and its budget share was never established; saying so explicitly is preferable to letting it
  silently consume a third of the campaign.

## Known differences from campaign N

Campaign N's masks are whole clusters; campaign O's are sub-cluster groups from a single committed
partition (`p9_grain.GROUP_SEED = 20260728`). The k=3 and k=5 partitions chunk the same per-cluster
permutation and 3 does not divide 5, so they cross-cut each other; both nest into k=15 only. Each
fresh rung therefore carries partition-sampling variance that k=15 structurally cannot, and that
caveat travels with the curve. A second partition draw is the cheap robustness check if the curve
comes out close.
